Quantum & Nuclear Physics — a core area of Physics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Quantum & Nuclear Physics brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Quantum & Nuclear Physics.

Does Hooke's law apply to a spring for any amount of stretching?
options: It becomes more elastic and can stretch further.
No — it only holds up to the limit of proportionality; beyond that the relationship between force and extension is no longer linear.
Yes — Hooke's law applies to any spring at any extension.
Only when the force is small enough to be ignored.

mcqs.q: What happens to a metal wire stretched beyond its elastic limit?
options: It snaps immediately at the elastic limit.
It becomes more elastic and can stretch further.
Only when the force is small enough to be ignored.
It deforms plastically and will not return to its original length when the load is removed.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between heat and temperature?
options: Heat is measured in degrees Celsius and temperature in Joules.
Heat and temperature are the same thing — both measure how hot something is.
Heat is the energy transferred due to temperature difference; temperature measures average kinetic energy of particles.
It becomes more elastic and can stretch further.
